plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit: if you bid higher than value, you risk winning at a loss; if you bid lower, you risk losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $15, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $15, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay a fair price when I do.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win. My value for this item is $0, meaning I have nothing to gain from winning - I would only lose money if I won since I'd have to pay whatever the second-highest bid is while gaining $0 in value. Therefore, I should bid exactly $0 to avoid any risk of winning and losing money.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies. Bidding above my value risks negative profit if I win at a price above my valuation; bidding below reduces my chance of winning profitable auctions. With a value of $45, I should bid exactly $45 to ensure optimal outcomes in all scenarios.
